summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old female with end-stage renal disease, hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy, and atrial flutter was admitted for recurrent substernal chest pain following hemodialysis. The pain was attributed to fluid shifts affecting her cardiac physiology. During the admission, she experienced an acute respiratory failure and PEA arrest requiring CPR, intubation, and ICU care. She recovered and was extubated, but developed musculoskeletal chest pain from chest compressions. An echo confirmed severe LVH with mild outflow obstruction, and a head CT showed small vessel ischemic disease and a nonspecific frontal lesion. Her INR was elevated at discharge, so warfarin was held. She was transitioned to a rehab facility for strength recovery with optimized medications, including increased metoprolol, addition of lisinopril, and dialysis modifications to limit fluid removal and include pre-treatment beta blockade.
